question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-party Control UI math-rendering implementation that adds same-origin third-party browser code, and what delimiter/config behavior is allowed by default?
rationale: The feature is useful and requested, but accepting global math parsing plus first-party execution of a vendored bundle changes compatibility and security posture in ways automation should not decide.

options.title: Track dependency and narrow parsing
options.body: Require package/build provenance or approved vendoring, avoid default single-dollar parsing, and land only after real Control UI proof.

options.title: Accept explicit vendoring
options.body: Maintainers can allow a vendored MathJax asset if the PR documents source, version, license, update process, and review ownership.

options.title: Defer this implementation
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and ask contributors to converge on a safer KaTeX/MathJax design before merging any candidate.

recommendation.title: Track dependency and narrow parsing
recommendation.body: Require package/build provenance or approved vendoring, avoid default single-dollar parsing, and land only after real Control UI proof.
